phase_name: River and Canal Intake and Pumping
physical_state_in: Natural surface water at river or reservoir
physical_state_out: Raw water at pump station outlet
D_parameters: WFD abstraction permit limits; minimum ecological flow requirements; seasonal demand curve; pump station rated capacity
C_parameters: agricultural demand from ~2.8M ha irrigated area; 78% surface water / 22% groundwater split
notes: Total agricultural abstraction 22 km3/yr = 63% of basin total. Largest single intake: Romania (~3.4 km3/yr from Danube main channel). AQUASTAT tracks annual abstraction by sector. EU members require WFD abstraction permits. Seasonal peak June-August. Opacity score 1.

physical_state_out: Water in primary canal or main pipeline
primary_transformation: Gravity flow or pressurized transport over tens to hundreds of km
measurable_output: Water delivered to primary distribution hubs
D_parameters: canal capacity constraints; sediment deposition; infrastructure age (avg 45 years); gradient limitations
C_parameters: water delivered to multiple irrigation blocks across large geographic areas; Romania; Hungary; Bulgaria; Serbia
notes: Primary canals total ~18000 km across the basin. Average conveyance losses 18% (unlined earth canals; seepage and evaporation). 60% earth canals; 40% concrete-lined. Infrastructure mostly built 1950-1975. EU CAP Pillar II funds some rehabilitation. Non-EU countries (Ukraine; Serbia; Bosnia) have very limited monitoring. Opacity score 3.

primary_transformation: Secondary canal and pipe network distributing to individual farms or irrigation blocks
D_parameters: pipe capacity; gate control precision; secondary canal maintenance state; field block boundary
C_parameters: farm-level delivery for multiple crop types; individual farm allocations
notes: Secondary and tertiary distribution is the least-monitored phase. Farm-level metering covers only ~35% of irrigated area across basin (EU 65%; non-EU 12%). Distribution losses 12-20% in unlined secondary canals. Secondary canal total ~85000 km. Remote sensing (MODIS ET; Landsat NDVI) provides indirect estimates. Opacity score 4 — most opaque phase.

physical_state_out: Water applied to crop root zone
primary_transformation: Field irrigation by gravity/flood; sprinkler; or drip method
typical_time_scale: Hours to days per irrigation event
D_parameters: crop water requirement (FAO Penman-Monteith); irrigation method efficiency ceiling; soil infiltration rate; scheduling
C_parameters: crop yield output; multiple crop types: maize (45%); wheat (20%); vegetables (15%); sunflower (10%); sugar beet (10%)
notes: Application efficiency: gravity/flood 47% (55% of area); sprinkler 75% (30%); drip 88% (15%). Weighted average ~50%. FAO Irrigation Paper 66 is primary benchmark. Eurostat tracks irrigation method by country (EU only). Remote sensing ET (GLEAM; SEBS) calibrates actual vs. potential ET. Opacity score 2.

physical_state_out: Drainage water returning to groundwater or river
primary_transformation: Gravity drainage to tile drains; ditches; and return canals
measurable_output: Return flow volume and nitrate load
D_parameters: drainage network capacity; environmental threshold constraints (EU Nitrates Directive 50 mg/l); phosphorus reduction targets
C_parameters: return flow of ~6.6 km3/yr (30% of abstraction) to groundwater and river system; nutrient and pesticide load to water bodies
notes: Agricultural drainage returns ~30% of abstracted water (6.6 km3/yr). Return flow carries significant pollution: nitrate avg 18 mg/l; 62% of Danube water bodies with agricultural diffuse pollution (ICPDR). EU Nitrates Directive monitoring in vulnerable zones. Phosphorus load ~85000 t/yr. 62% of monitored water bodies have detected pesticide residues. Opacity score 2.
